# Introduction

Every model in `diseasy` contains some parameterisation of its forecasts.
These parameters can then be optimised to align model forecasts with the
real-world observations.

This operation requires only two components:
1) A metric for the optimiser to optimise
2) Free parameters for the optimiser to control

# The scoring metric
The principal metric used in `diseasy` is the likelihood which compares the
model forecast with observations for each time-point at each strata and computes
the mean likelihood across the strata for the given time-point.

Different observation have different distributions and therefore `diseasy`
supports multiple methods for computing the likelihood given the underlying
(assumed) distribution.

The scoring of the forecasts are controlled by the `?DiseasyScoring` module,
where users can define the scoring metric and which includes a method to
compute the likelihood for a given set of model trajectories
(i.e. the output from `$get_results()`).

```{r DiseasyScoring}
scoring <- DiseasyScoring$new()

scoring
```

The scoring metric can be controlled with the `?DiseasyScoring$set_noise_model()`
method:
```{r DiseasyScoring - negative binomial}
scoring$set_noise_model("negative binomial", overdispersion = 2)

scoring
```

With the scoring metric defined, we can compute the likelihood for a set of
model trajectories with `?DiseasyScoring$compute_likelihood()`:

```{r DiseasyScoring - compute_likelihood, eval = rlang::is_installed("duckdb")}
observables <- DiseasyObservables$new(
  diseasystore = "simulist",
  conn = \() DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), ":memory:")
)

observables$set_last_queryable_date(as.Date("2020-03-01"))

model <- DiseasyModelG0$new(
  observables = observables
)

trajectories <- model$get_results(observable = "n_admission", prediction_length = 7)

model$scoring$compute_likelihood(trajectories)
```
